data.source_title: Omitting Routine Radiography of Traumatic Distal Radial Fractures After Initial 2-Week Follow-up Does Not Affect Outcomes
data.locator: Abstract, lines 41-59; Methods, design/setting and inclusion/exclusion, PDF pp.2-3, lines 105-133; Results, PDF pp.1 and 7-8, lines 49-58 and 361-368.
data.source_setting: Four level-I trauma centers in the Netherlands; multicenter prospective randomized non-inferiority trial of adult traumatic distal-radius fractures.
data.source_period: Enrollment dates not stated in inspected article; publication year 2019.
data.source_n: 386 randomized; 326 analyzed (usual care n=166, reduced-imaging n=160).
data.quantity: Outcomes when routine radiographs at 6 and 12 weeks were omitted after initial two-week follow-up
data.unit: percent; radiographs per patient (median); qualitative comparison
data.source_evidence_basis: The randomized trial reported comparable DASH and secondary outcomes and similar complication rates after reduced imaging; participants still received clinical and radiographic review up to two weeks.
data.limitations: 326 of 386 randomized participants were analyzed; open Gustilo grade 2/3 fractures and multiple extremity fractures were excluded. Netherlands care setting and intervention do not validate a US site schedule or establish safety for unstable/high-risk individual cases.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Keep early alignment review distinct from later routine imaging. Treat the trial as evidence about one follow-up strategy, not proof that an individual needs no further assessment.
